name: Mk2
summary: Rebuilt around stability. Larger fins and a longer nose with a ballast pocket, checked in simulation first.

parts.description: Tangent ogive nose cone, printed as a hollow shell with a shoulder that locates in the avionics bay. A removable ballast pocket lets the CG be trimmed.
parts.changeNote: 40 mm longer, with a removable ballast pocket for trimming the centre of gravity.

parts.description: Sealed bay for the flight data logger. The exposed band carries the static vent holes; the spigot is the friction-fit separation joint with the recovery tube.
Sealed bulkheads keep ejection gas away from the electronics and the barometer.
Removable sled holding the logger; slides out at the field for data download and battery changes.
Arduino Nano-size board running the data-logging firmware: fixed-rate logging, launch/apogee/landing detection and an altitude beep-out after landing.
parts.label: Flight data logger

parts.description: Pressure sensor used for altitude. It reads the static pressure through the vent holes.
Accelerometer (±16 g) and gyroscope, axes aligned with the rocket.
Sized for over an hour armed on the pad, strapped down for 15–20 g.
External switch so the logger can be armed on the pad without opening the bay.
Forward shock cord anchor through the aft bulkhead.
Upper body tube housing the parachute, shock cord and protector.
Links the nose/av-bay to the aft section after ejection.
Size to be set with the MATLAB simulator (target landing speed 6 m/s or less).
parts.label: Parachute

parts.description: Shields the parachute from the hot ejection charge gases.
parts.label: Chute protector

parts.description: Lower body tube with through-the-wall fin slots and rail button holes.
parts.label: Aft body tube

parts.description: 29 mm motor mount tube; carries thrust into the airframe.
Centres the motor tube in the body tube. The fin tabs are bonded between the two rings.
parts.label: Centring ring

parts.description: The motor pushes on this ring, so thrust goes into the motor tube rather than the motor sliding forward.
The motor has not been chosen yet. A 29 mm G-class dummy is shown for sizing, and its mass is an estimate.
parts.label: Motor (not chosen yet)

parts.description: Screw-on retainer so the ejection charge pushes the parachute out, not the motor.
Through-the-wall fins, to be sized for a 1–2 caliber stability margin.
parts.changeNote: Span up from 34 mm to 55 mm and a longer root, which moves the centre of pressure aft.

parts.description: Guides the rocket along the launch rail until it is fast enough to be stable.
Aft shock cord attachment on the forward centring ring.

changes.title: Larger fins
changes.detail: Fin span increased from 34 mm to 55 mm and the root chord from 70 mm to 100 mm.
changes.why: Bigger fins move the centre of pressure towards the tail, which raises the stability margin.

changes.title: Longer nose with a ballast pocket
changes.detail: The nose cone is 40 mm longer and has a removable pocket for small weights.
changes.why: Weight in the nose moves the centre of gravity forward, and the pocket means it can be adjusted at the field.

changes.title: Simulated before flying
changes.detail: Stability and expected apogee were checked in a flight simulation before the airframe was glued.
changes.why: Mk1 flew on a guess. A simulation would have caught the problem on the ground.

buildLog.title: Redesign after Mk1
buildLog.text: Worked through the Mk1 flight data and rebuilt the fin and nose geometry around a target margin of 1.5 or more.

buildLog.title: New fins cut and fitted
buildLog.text: Fins cut from the same 3 mm ply. Alignment jig printed to hold all three square while the glue set.

buildLog.title: Balance check
buildLog.text: Measured the centre of gravity on a knife edge with the motor fitted. Added 12 g of ballast in the nose pocket.

flights.title: Flight 1
flights.notes: Straight, stable climb. The parachute came out several seconds after apogee, with the rocket already falling fast. It landed hard and split a fin at the root.

failure.what: The parachute deployed late. The rocket was already descending quickly, so it hit the ground harder than the airframe could take.
failure.rootCause: Apogee was detected from a single pressure sensor. A pressure disturbance inside the bay near apogee was read as continued climb, which delayed the deployment signal.
failure.evidence: The altitude log shows peak height about three seconds before the deployment event. One fin split along the grain at the root on landing.

todo.text: Detect apogee in a way that one noisy reading cannot delay

Reach the 500 m target (Mk2 peaked short of it)
